notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR6: 'Integer-1 may be signed and, if signed, it must be positive', with §1985:III.2's 'neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed' for zero. VersionConformancePass.VisitSubscriptPart asks Cobol85OperandForms.IsSubscript of every subscript of a data reference (including a qualified one and a function argument), which takes integer-1 through IsInteger with Cobol85IntegerSign.Positive (a + sign touching nonzero integer digits passes; - , zero at any sign, a fraction or a detached sign fail), and anything else is the 2002 arithmetic-expression construct, COBOL0900 at 85. The witness writes ELEM (-1). Probes at 85: refused (-2), (+0), (0), (-0), (+1.0), (- 1), CELL (1, -1), a condition-name ISABC (-1) in IF and SET, ELEM (-1) (1:1), an ODO element OE (-3), FUNCTION LENGTH (ELEM (-1)), ELEM OF TBL (-1), N - -1, N + +1; accepted (+1), CELL (+2, +1), (+000000000000000002) and N + 1, each printing the right element; at 2023 ELEM (-2) compiles (c).

next.reason: 1985 SR6: 'Integer-1 may be signed and, if signed, it must be positive', a compile-time refusal of a negative literal subscript. In 2023 a literal subscript is an arithmetic-expression-1 (§2023:8.4.2.3.2), and no syntax rule limits its sign. §2023:8.4.2.3.4 GR2: 'If the value of the subscript is not a positive integer or is less than one', the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT exception condition is set to exist. The refusal became a run-time exception condition (error mode c).
